--- C-1233_complaint.pdf, page 1 ---
 Harris County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0023
 Warren Fletcher, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Plaintiff's Original Petition
Filed:
July 23, 2024
Plaintiff's counsel:
Kyle Sanders, Marshall & Dominguez LLP
PARTIES
Plaintiff is Warren Fletcher, an individual who resides in Texas and who was the driver of a passenger vehicle involved in the
collision described below. Defendant is the automobile liability insurer that issued the policy under which Plaintiff seeks
coverage and benefits. Defendant may be served through its registered agent for service of process in accordance with the Texas
Rules of Civil Procedure.
FACTS
On December 27, 2023, Plaintiff was lawfully operating a vehicle in League City while turning left at an intersection. While
Plaintiff's vehicle was in the process of completing the turn, a second vehicle traveling in the opposite direction struck the side of
Plaintiff's car. The impact caused Plaintiff's vehicle to rotate and strike a roadside barrier. Plaintiff reported the collision to
Defendant promptly and submitted the required claim documentation, including a statement describing how the crash occurred.
Defendant's adjuster later informed Plaintiff that the claim was under review but has not issued a fair resolution of the claim.
NEGLIGENCE
The driver of the other vehicle failed to yield the right-of-way, failed to keep a proper lookout, and failed to control speed, in
violation of the Texas Transportation Code. That neglignece proximately caused the collision and Plaintiff's resulting injuries.
Defendant, as the insurer obligated to pay covered benefits under the policy, owed Plaintiff a duty to investigate the claim in good
faith, to evaluate it fairly, and to pay amounts due within a reasonable time. Defendant breached those duties by delaying its
investigation without reasonable basis, failing to offer a settlement reflecting the clear liability facts, and failing to explain its
position in writing as Texas law requires.
DAMAGES
As a direct result of the collision, Plaintiff suffered a fracture of the wrist, requiring medical treatment, immobilization, and
ongoing therapy. Plaintiff has incurred medical expenses, lost wages from time away from work, and continuing pain and
reduced function in the hand and wrist. Plaintiff seeks recovery of all damages allowed by Texas law, including actual damages,
economic losses, and, where applicable, statutory interest and attorney's fees. Plaintiff demands payment in the amount of
$68,000.00.

Kyle Sanders
Marshall & Dominguez LLP

--- C-1233_defense_answer.pdf, page 1 ---
 Harris County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0023
 Warren Fletcher, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Defendant's Original Answer
Date:
9-3-24
Counsel for defendant:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict
proof thereof by a preponderance of the evidence, as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.
Subject to and without waiving the foregoing general denial, Defendant asserts the following affirmative defenses.
First, Plaintiff's own negligence caused or contributed to the collision. Plaintiff failed to keep a proper lookout, failed to
yield the right-of-way, and failed to exercise ordinary care under the circumstances, and any recovery must be
reduced in proportion to Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and
Remedies Code.
Second, the collision was proximately caused by the acts or omissions of a third party over whom Defendant had no
control, and that third party's conduct constitutes a new and independent cause of Plaintiff's alleged injuries.
Third, Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by not following reasonable medical advice and by incurring medical
expenses that were unnecessary or unreasonable in amount, and any recovery must be limited accordingly.
Defendant reserves the right to amend this answer as discovery proceeds.

--- C-1233_deposition.pdf, page 1 ---
 Harris County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0023
 Warren Fletcher, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Warren Fletcher
Date:
January 29, 2025
Location:
Offices of Marshall & Dominguez LLP
Examining attorney:
Marilyn Fox, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Kyle Sanders, Marshall & Dominguez LLP
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a transcript, but you can refer to me as the plaintiff.
Q: Understood. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving through League City, Texas, heading to a shop on the north side of town. I was making a left turn at an
intersection with a traffic signal.
Q: What happened when you started the turn?
A: I had a green arrow, or at least I believed I did. I started into the intersection and a pickup coming the other way struck the
front driver's side of my car.
Q: Did you see the pickup before the impact?
A: Not clearly. I remember a glare from the headlights and then a loud bang. I didn't have time to brake.
Q: What did you do immediately after the collision?
A: I sat for a moment because my hand was throbbing. A bystander came over and asked if I was okay. Then I called my husband
and waited for the police to arrive.
Q: Did you seek medical care that day?
A: Yes. I was taken by ambulance to a local emergency room. They took X-rays and told me my wrist was broken.
Q: What was the diagnosis?
A: A fracture of the wrist on my dominant side. They put it in a splint and referred me to an orthopedic specialist.
Q: Have you had surgery or other procedures since then?
A: I had a follow-up visit where the doctor decided a cast was enough at first. Later I was told I might need physical therapy, and
I have been attending sessions twice a week.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Simple things are hard. Buttoning a shirt, opening jars, and typing for work all take much longer. I had to ask a coworker to
help me carry boxes, and I haven't been able to drive for several weeks without discomfort.
Q: Have you missed time from work?
A: Yes, I took a few weeks off, and I've been working reduced hours since then while my hand heals.
Q: Have you experienced any pain or limitations that persist today?
A: Yes. Cold weather makes it ache, and I still get sharp pain when I grip something heavy. My therapist says improvement is
happening, but it's slower than I hoped.
